entities.summary: Peter III of Arborea, Judge of Arborea (1335-1347 CE), played a pivotal role in the history of medieval Italy. As the firstborn son of Hugh II, he assumed the throne upon his father's death and ruled until his own demise in 1347 CE. During his reign, Peter III implemented various judicial reforms, enhancing the governance of Arborea and solidifying its position as a key player in the Mediterranean region. His legacy continued to shape the island's politics and society for generations to come. A testament to his enduring influence can be seen in the continued relevance of the Arborean judicial system, which remains a model for modern-day legal frameworks. The exact date of Peter III's birth is unknown, adding a layer of mystery to his already fascinating story. Despite the passing of centuries, his impact on the history of Arborea and the broader Mediterranean world remains a subject of interest among historians and scholars alike.
